title: Thomas Tuchel’s England’s Left Back Options—Ranked
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Barnaby LaneSep 9, 2025Tuchel loves Lewis Hall. /  Eddie Keogh/Getty ImagesUnder Sir Gareth Southgate, the left side of England’s defense was a persistent problem.

Luke Shaw and Ben Chilwell were the two primary options, but recurring injury issues regularly limited their availability and left the Three Lions short of reliable cover. Thomas Tuchel, currently overseeing a period of transition in the national team, has a considerably deeper pool of talent to work with.

The German coach has several players capable of filling the role, from attack-minded, traditional left backs to versatile midfielders who can drop into defense and center backs comfortable operating on the left. With so many possibilities at his disposal, Tuchel has no shortage of options to consider when putting together his defensive lineup.
Here’s Sports Illustrated’s ranking of England’s left back candidates and examination of what each brings to the table.

Lewis-Skelly can play in midfield, too. / Eddie Keogh/Getty ImagesMyles Lewis-Skelly can operate at both left back and in midfield, although it’s arguably in the latter role where he thrives most and certainly where he gets the majority of his minutes for Arsenal. His combative nature and ability to retain possession are attributes that serve him particularly well in the middle of the park.That same tenacity, however, can prove useful when he’s called upon on the left side of defense, making him a solid alternative for England when other options aren’t available.

Livramento missed out on his first World Cup. / Bradley Collyer/PA Images/Getty ImagesTino Livramento is naturally a right back, but spent a significant amount of time filling in at left back for the injured Lewis Hall during his time at Newcastle—and has made it look incredibly easy.Comfortable on both feet and confident cutting inside in the final third, the former Chelsea youngster is a classy operator on either flank. His history of recurring injuries remains a concern.

Dan Burn is rock solid. / Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesBefore you bite our head off, we know Dan Burn is primarily a center back—but he has often covered admirably for Newcastle United at left back when injuries have struck.He’s hardly the type to bomb forward and whip crosses into the box, but when it comes to sheer defensive solidity, few do it better.

Djed Spence has enjoyed quite the career turnaround. / Eston Parker/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesNot long ago, Djed Spence wouldn’t have even been part of this conversation.A couple of standout campaigns with Tottenham, followed by an impressive 2026 World Cup, have changed that. After a difficult start to the tournament, Spence emerged as one of England’s top performers, earning starts against both Argentina and France and impressing with his electric pace, energy in the final third and ability to recover possession.Now at Inter Milan, Spence has established himself as a brilliant two-way operator, and few can question his credentials anymore.

Lewis Hall knows how to deliver a cross. / Florencia Tan Jun/Getty ImagesThere is no doubting Lewis Hall’s ability.The Newcastle United man has everything you’d want from a modern left back: defensive nous, pace, the ability to get forward and a wicked end product in the final third.Injury setbacks have disrupted his progress, while Newcastle’s own struggles have arguably done him few favors in recent times. However, you can’t help but feel that if he can stay fit and perhaps even secure a move to a bigger club, the sky is the limit.

O'Reilly is England's best left back. / Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty ImagesPep Guardiola loved an inverted fullback, and Nico Reilly was his final creation in that role at Manchester City. The former midfielder was transformed into an electric left back capable of defending, carrying the ball forward and contributing to the build-up play when moving inside.The youngster was one of City’s standout performers during Guardiola’s final season, scoring an impressive nine goals across all competitions—including both goals in the 2–0 EFL Cup final win over Arsenal.
